verdict.rationale: The docs say pre-built llamafiles are provided that run immediately: download, make executable, run, as a single portable executable on Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD with no installation (docs-3, docs-19, docs-16, gh-3). Hands-on users confirm it worked first try on Linux, and the author says stock Windows CPU inference needs no dev tools (comm-6, comm-1). Caveats: early GPU acceleration on Windows required local compilation with CUDA/MSVC, which failed for one user (comm-2), and Windows caps executables at 4GB, which hits large prebuilt files (comm-14, comm-18). Missing for 10: evidence of distribution through package managers (e.g. Homebrew or apt), and independent confirmation that current GPU acceleration ships fully precompiled without local toolchains.
